name: fchown
synopsis: int fchown(int fd, uid_t owner, gid_t group);
description: fchown() changes the ownership of the file referred to by the open file descriptor fd. Only a privileged process can change the owner, and the owner can change the group to any group they are a member of. If the owner or group is specified as -1, that ID is not changed.

parameters.name: fd
parameters.description: File descriptor of the file to change ownership.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: The user ID of the new owner, or -1 to leave unchanged.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: The group ID of the new group, or -1 to leave unchanged.

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: Search permission is denied on a component of the path prefix.
fd is not a valid open file descriptor.
pathname points outside your accessible address space.
A low-level I/O error occurred while modifying the inode.
Too many symbolic links were encountered in resolving pathname.
A component of the path prefix is not a directory.
The calling process did not have the required permissions to change owner and/or group, or the file is marked immutable or append-only.
The named file resides on a read-only filesystem.

versions: Since glibc 2.12 with _POSIX_C_SOURCE >= 200809L or _XOPEN_SOURCE >= 500, or _BSD_SOURCE for glibc <= 2.19
